subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme A · Organisms & Ecosystems (Diversity, Evolution, Conservation)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The human species is correctly written in binomial nomenclature as:
questions.explain: Genus capitalised, species epithet lower case, both italicised.

questions.q: A biological species is a group of organisms that:
options: Can interbreed to produce fertile offspring
questions.explain: The biological species concept centres on interbreeding to produce fertile offspring.

questions.q: A dichotomous key identifies organisms using:
options: A series of paired, contrasting choices
questions.explain: Each step offers two contrasting options until the organism is identified.

questions.q: Biodiversity includes species diversity, ecosystem diversity and:
questions.explain: Biodiversity spans genetic variation, species variety and ecosystem range.

questions.q: Natural selection requires all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explain: Darwinian selection acts on heritable variation, not on characteristics acquired during life.

questions.q: In evolutionary terms, fitness means an organism's:
questions.explain: Fitness is the ability to survive and reproduce, passing on alleles.

questions.q: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria spreading over time is an example of:
questions.explain: Antibiotics select for pre-existing resistant variants that survive and reproduce.

questions.q: Homologous structures such as the pentadactyl limb provide evidence of:
questions.explain: Shared structure with different functions indicates descent from a common ancestor.

questions.q: Allopatric speciation begins with:
questions.explain: A physical barrier separates populations, which then diverge until reproductively isolated.

questions.q: Two populations are regarded as separate species once they show:
questions.explain: Speciation is complete when populations can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

questions.q: Which provides fossil-independent evidence for evolution?
questions.explain: Artificial selection shows how heritable change accumulates rapidly under selection.

questions.q: In-situ conservation means conserving species:
questions.explain: Nature reserves and national parks protect species within functioning ecosystems.

questions.q: An example of ex-situ conservation is:
questions.explain: Ex-situ methods conserve organisms outside their natural habitat (zoos, seed banks).

questions.q: A keystone species is one that:
options: Has a disproportionately large effect on its community
questions.explain: Removing a keystone species can greatly change community structure.

questions.q: The leading current cause of biodiversity loss worldwide is:
questions.explain: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the main driver, alongside climate change and overexploitation.

questions.q: The EDGE programme prioritises species that are:
questions.explain: EDGE targets species both distinct on the tree of life and at high extinction risk.

questions.q: A selection pressure is:
options: An environmental factor affecting survival and reproduction
questions.explain: Selection pressures favour some phenotypes over others.

questions.q: Variation within a species is important because it:
options: Provides the raw material for natural selection
questions.explain: Without heritable variation there is nothing for selection to act on.

questions.q: Higher biodiversity generally makes an ecosystem:
questions.explain: Diversity provides functional redundancy, aiding recovery from disturbance.

questions.q: Speciation by polyploidy, common in plants, occurs without geographic separation and is therefore:
questions.explain: Polyploidy can create instant reproductive isolation within the same area.
